text: When Jesus had finished all this teaching, he told his disciples,
"You know Passover is two days off — and the Son of Man is about to be handed over to be crucified."
Around that time the chief priests and elders gathered at the residence of the high priest, Caiaphas,
and plotted how to arrest Jesus quietly and put him to death.
"Not during the festival," they agreed, "or the crowd will riot."
While Jesus was in Bethany, at the house of Simon, a man who'd had leprosy,
a woman came up with an alabaster jar of very expensive perfume and poured it over his head as he reclined at the table.
The disciples were indignant when they saw it. "What a waste," they said.
"This could have been sold for a great deal and given to the poor."
Jesus noticed and said, "Why are you bothering her? She's done something beautiful for me.
The poor will always be with you, but you won't always have me.
By pouring this perfume on my body, she has prepared me for burial.
Truly I tell you, wherever this good news is preached in all the world, what she has done will be told in memory of her."
Then one of the Twelve, the one called Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests
and asked, "What will you give me if I hand him over to you?" They counted out thirty silver coins for him.
From then on he watched for the right moment to betray Jesus.
On the first day of Unleavened Bread the disciples came to Jesus and asked, "Where do you want us to prepare the Passover meal for you?"
"Go into the city," he told them, "to a certain man, and tell him: The Teacher says, My time is near — I'm keeping the Passover at your house with my disciples."
The disciples did as Jesus directed and prepared the Passover.
When evening came, he sat down to eat with the Twelve.
While they were eating he said, "Truly I tell you, one of you will betray me."
Deeply troubled, each of them began to ask, "Surely not I, Lord?"
He answered, "The one who has dipped his hand in the bowl with me will betray me.
The Son of Man goes on as it is written of him, but woe to the man who betrays him — better if he had never been born."
Judas, the betrayer, spoke up: "Surely not I, Rabbi?" Jesus told him, "You have said it yourself."
As they ate, Jesus took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples, saying, "Take this and eat it; this is my body."
Then he took a cup, gave thanks, and gave it to them, saying, "All of you drink from it.
This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.
I tell you, I won't drink this fruit of the vine again until the day I drink it new with you in my Father's kingdom."
After singing a hymn, they went out to the Mount of Olives.
Jesus told them, "Tonight all of you will fall away because of me, for it's written: I will strike the shepherd and the sheep will scatter.
But after I'm raised up, I'll go ahead of you to Galilee."
Peter said to him, "Even if everyone else falls away, I never will."
Jesus replied, "Truly I tell you, this very night, before the rooster crows, you'll deny me three times."
"Even if I have to die with you," Peter said, "I'll never deny you." All the disciples said the same.
Then Jesus came with them to a place called Gethsemane, and told the disciples, "Sit here while I go over there and pray."
He took along Peter and the two sons of Zebedee, and began to feel sorrow and distress.
"My soul is crushed with sorrow, to the point of death," he told them. "Stay here and keep watch with me."
Going a little further, he fell facedown and prayed, "My Father, if it's possible, let this cup pass from me — yet not as I will, but as you will."
He came back to the disciples and found them sleeping. "Couldn't you stay awake with me one hour?" he asked Peter.
"Stay awake and pray so you won't fall into temptation. The spirit is willing, but the flesh is weak."
He went away a second time and prayed, "My Father, if this cup cannot pass unless I drink it, your will be done."
When he returned he found them asleep again; their eyes were heavy.
So he left them once more and prayed a third time, saying the same words.
Then he came to the disciples and said, "Still sleeping? Still resting? Look, the hour has come, and the Son of Man is about to be handed over to sinners.
Get up, let's go. Here comes the one who is betraying me."
While he was still speaking, Judas, one of the Twelve, arrived with a large crowd armed with swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests and elders.
The betrayer had arranged a signal: "The one I kiss is the man — arrest him."
Judas went right up to Jesus and said, "Greetings, Rabbi!" and kissed him.
Jesus said, "Friend, do what you came to do." Then the men stepped in, seized Jesus, and arrested him.
One of Jesus' companions drew a sword, struck the high priest's servant, and cut off his ear.
"Put your sword back," Jesus told him. "Everyone who lives by the sword will die by the sword.
Don't you think I could call on my Father, and he'd send more than twelve legions of angels right now?
But then how would the Scriptures be fulfilled, which say it must happen this way?"
At that moment Jesus said to the crowd, "Did you come with swords and clubs to arrest me like an outlaw? I sat teaching in the temple courts every day, and you didn't lay a hand on me.
But all of this has happened so the writings of the prophets would be fulfilled." Then all the disciples deserted him and fled.
Those who had arrested Jesus led him to Caiaphas the high priest, where the scribes and elders had gathered.
Peter followed at a distance as far as the high priest's courtyard, went in, and sat with the guards to see how it would end.
The chief priests and the whole council looked for false testimony against Jesus so they could put him to death,
but they found none, even though many false witnesses came forward. Finally two men stepped up
and said, "This man said, I can tear down God's temple and rebuild it in three days."
The high priest stood and asked Jesus, "Have you no answer to what these men are testifying against you?"
Jesus stayed silent. So the high priest said, "I put you under oath by the living God — tell us if you are the Messiah, the Son of God."
"You have said it," Jesus replied. "And I tell you, from now on you'll see the Son of Man seated at the right hand of the Power and coming on the clouds of heaven."
At that the high priest tore his robes and said, "He has blasphemed! Why do we need more witnesses? You've just heard the blasphemy.
What's your verdict?" "He deserves death," they answered.
Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists. Others slapped him
and said, "Prophesy to us, Messiah — who hit you?"
Meanwhile Peter was sitting outside in the courtyard when a servant girl came up and said, "You were with Jesus the Galilean too."
He denied it in front of everyone. "I don't know what you're talking about," he said.
When he went out to the gateway, another servant girl saw him and told the people there, "This man was with Jesus of Nazareth."
Again he denied it, this time with an oath: "I don't know the man!"
A little later the bystanders came up and said to Peter, "You must be one of them — your accent gives you away."
Then he began to curse and swear, "I don't know the man!" — and immediately a rooster crowed.
Peter remembered what Jesus had said: "Before the rooster crows, you'll deny me three times." He went outside and wept bitterly.
